issues.legal_issue: An allotment made without notifying the landlord of the allotment proceedings is illegal.
material_facts: The authority reconsidered applications to allot a vacant part of a building after an earlier allotment had been set aside.
By then, a new landlord owned the building and occupied another part of it, but the authority did not notify him of the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The failure to notify the landlord as required by the applicable rules rendered the allotment order illegal.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 9(3) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Rules, 1972 requires notice to the landlord of the date fixed for considering allotment. Notice enables the landlord to object, seek release, or, where applicable, nominate a tenant. An allotment made without that notice is illegal. The Court relied on Yoginder Tiwari v. District Judge, Gorakhpur and Ors.

predicates.rental_allotment_proceeding: An authority is considering applications to allot a vacant rental building or part of one.
predicates.a_vacant_part_is_considered: A building or part of a building has fallen vacant or is likely to fall vacant and is being considered for allotment.
predicates.landlord_notified_of_allotment_hearing_i: The landlord was not given notice of the date on which the allotment would be considered.

issues.definition: When a rental allotment proceeding considers a vacant part and the landlord is not notified of the hearing, the allotment order is illegal.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord occupying one part of a building is entitled to nominate the tenant for another part being allotted, and the authority must provide an opportunity to exercise that right.
material_facts: The landlord occupied the ground floor of the building while the first floor was considered for allotment.
The authority knew that the landlord occupied part of the building but gave him no opportunity to nominate a tenant before allotting the first floor to the appellant.
issues.conclusion: The landlord was entitled to nominate a tenant of his choice, and the allotment made without affording that opportunity was without jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17(2) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 requires allotment of another part of a building in favour of a person nominated by the landlord when the landlord occupies a part for residential purposes. The authority must afford the landlord the opportunity to nominate, and must allot to the nominee if one is put forward. The Court relied on Babu Singh Chauhan v. Rajkumar Jain & Ors. and also discussed the notice requirement in Yoginder Tiwari v. District Judge, Gorakhpur and Ors.

predicates.rental_allotment_proceeding: An authority is considering applications to allot a vacant rental building or part of one.
predicates.landlord_occupies_another_part_for_resid: The landlord occupies another part of the same building for residential purposes.
predicates.landlord_denied_opportunity_to_nominate: The landlord was not given an opportunity to nominate a tenant before the authority made the allotment.

issues.definition: If a residential rental allotment concerns a vacant part of a building whose landlord resides in another part, the landlord must be given an opportunity to nominate a tenant.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee landlord who occupies part of a building retains the right to nominate a tenant for another part even if the former landlord's application for release was rejected.
material_facts: The former landlord's application to have the vacant first floor released to him had been rejected before he sold the building.
The transferee acquired the building, occupied the ground floor, and became its landlord before the allotment applications were reconsidered.
The transferee was not given an opportunity to nominate a tenant for the first floor.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the former landlord's release application did not prevent the transferee landlord from exercising the right to nominate a tenant.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 17(2) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, a landlord occupying a part of a building for residential purposes may nominate a tenant for another part being allotted. The Court held that the transferee landlord could exercise that right despite the former landlord's unsuccessful release application; it relied on Babu Singh Chauhan v. Rajkumar Jain & Ors. in explaining the purpose of the nomination right.

predicates.rental_allotment_proceeding: An authority is reconsidering applications to allot a vacant rental building or part of one.
predicates.former_landlord_release_request_was_reje: The former landlord's request to have the vacant premises released to him was rejected.
predicates.transferee_became_landlord_before_recons: A person acquired the building and became its landlord before the allotment applications were reconsidered.
predicates.transferee_occupies_part_for_residence: The transferee landlord occupies another part of the same building for residential purposes.

issues.definition: When a transferee becomes landlord before allotment is reconsidered and resides in another part of the building, rejection of the former landlord's release request does not remove the transferee's right to nominate a tenant.

issues.legal_issue: A procedural defect in entertaining a review application does not warrant disturbing a recall of an allotment order that was illegal for failure to comply with a mandatory requirement.
material_facts: The authority recalled an allotment order because the landlord had not been notified and had been denied the opportunity to nominate a tenant.
The reviewing court had upheld the recall, and the allotment order was illegal for non-compliance with the mandatory requirement governing the landlord's nomination right.
The appellant challenged the recall, including on the ground that the review application was procedurally defective.
issues.conclusion: Even if there was a procedural defect in entertaining the review application, it was not proper or desirable to interfere with the recall of the illegal allotment order.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied section 17(2) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, under which the landlord's nomination right is mandatory, and reasoned that a procedural defect in review did not justify restoring an allotment made in violation of that requirement, particularly when the High Court had upheld the recall.

predicates.appeal_challenging_recall_of_allotment: An appeal challenges an authority's decision to recall an allotment order.
predicates.original_allotment_violated_mandatory_la: The original allotment was made without complying with a mandatory right of the landlord.
predicates.reviewing_court_upheld_recall: A reviewing court upheld the authority's decision to recall the allotment.

issues.definition: In an appeal challenging a recall, a procedural defect in review does not justify disturbing the recall when the original allotment violated a mandatory landlord right and a reviewing court upheld the recall.
